concerns.text: FR-002 requires training Decision Trees on CPU-only hardware. T005b implements CLIP/FID metrics but lacks an explicit CPU-only enforcement (e.g., `device='cpu'` or `set_device('cpu')`) in the metric calculation logic, risking silent GPU usage on the free-tier runner as flagged in the analyze report.

FR-001 requires generating a dataset from a sampled subset of ImageNet/LAION. T012 assumes pre-fetched data and exits with code 1 if missing, contradicting Spec Assumption A1 which allows for a 'pre-computed dataset' fallback or separate GPU resource. There is no task to handle the 'pre-computed dataset' scenario or to implement the streaming fetch if pre-fetch fails, blocking the project if data is not manually pre-fetched.

FR-004 requires re-running the selected expert field to generate a NEW velocity vector based on tree prediction. T029a states 'Do NOT use the pre-computed teacher vector' but fails to explicitly link this regenerated vector to the Euler integrator (T029c) in the subsequent image generation step, creating a gap where the pipeline might default to the teacher's vector.

SC-005 mandates a hard stop-early condition if the 6-hour runtime is exceeded. T030c only calculates sample size and sets a flag if time is running out; it does not enforce the stop-early condition for the training loop (T021) or the evaluation loop, contradicting the requirement to 'stop early and report results for completed depths'.

FR-001 requires generating a dataset from a 'sampled subset'. T012b hardcodes a target of '2500 raw samples' without a mechanism to dynamically adjust based on data availability or the 'sampled subset' definition, potentially violating the '≥1,000 rows' acceptance criterion if the source data is insufficient.

SC-004 requires measuring the relationship between `max_depth` and routing accuracy against a 'saturation point'. T021 trains trees for `range(2, 21)` (depths 2 to 20); this arbitrary upper bound may miss the actual saturation point if the model requires a depth > 20 to plateau, leading to an inconclusive result for SC-004.

FR-005 requires evaluating ALL samples (matched and mismatched) to capture total system error. T030d performs statistical tests without explicitly specifying that the input data must include the *mismatched* samples, risking a bias towards only 'matched' cases if the data filtering in T029a/T028b inadvertently excludes them.

Constitution Principle I (Reproducibility) requires fetching external datasets from the same canonical source on every run. T042 implements a real data fetcher but lacks a requirement to cache the *exact* fetched stream hash (via `state/...yaml`) to ensure that a re-run on a fresh runner fetches the *identical* bytes, not just 'the same source' which might have drifted.
